newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - March 26.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- COUNTRY CASUALS FACES FRESH TAKEOVER BID BY MANAGEMENT

Country Casuals, the womenswear group, admitted it could face a takeover bid from Mark Bunce, its chief executive, just 14 months after foiling a bid from its former chairman, John Shannon. Bunce is in preliminary talks about making an offer for the company, along with his wife and fellow director. It is unclear if the couple have secured any financing for the offer. Andrew Mills-Baker, finance director, said the board would look at any offer that may improve shareholder value.
-- LITTLEWOODS TO RETREAT FROM MOSCOW

Littlewoods is to pull out of retailing in Russia by selling its four Russian stores, six years after becoming the first Western retailer to open shops there. Stores will also be sold in Bangalore, India, which were opened last year. If a buyer cannot be found the stores will be shut down and Littlewoods may be forced to make provisions to cover the closure costs. The group's international business has lost money due to start-up costs.
-- SCOTIA UP ON CANCER DRUG TEST RESULTS

The biotechnology company which develops drugs based on evening primrose oil, Scotia, has announced positive results for its Foscan cancer drug. The company is beginning phase III clinical trials of the drug in head, neck and laryngeal cancers this spring. The company has also signed an agreement with Ajinomoto, the Japanese food group, to develop and market SC103, its drug for diabetic complications, giving Scotia an undisclosed up-front fee.
THE TIMES
-- NATIONAL SAVINGS CRITICISED OVER 50 MILLION STG 'BLACK HOLE'

A report published by the Select Committee of Public Accountants, an all-party group of MPs, has blamed a 50 million stg accounting black hole and other discrepancies on "deplorable" laxness at the National Savings arm. National Savings manages 57 billion stg and the report suggests it had failed to heed warnings of fundamental problems in its "seriously inadequate" financial control programme.
-- PRU WINS SCOTAM WITH OFFER OF 2.1 BILLION STG

Prudential Corporation has succeeded in its 2.15 billion stg bid for Scottish Amicable, the mutual life insurer. Scottish Amicable policyholders are set to share a 1.5 billion stg cash- and-bonus package. The Pru is paying 850 million stg from shareholders' and policyholders' funds. Of this, 600 million stg will be paid in cash to policyholders on completion of the deal and a further 250 million stg in bonuses over the life of policies.
-- QUARTER-POINT RISE FOR U.S. RATES

The Federal Open Market Committee has raised U.S. interest rates by a quarter percentage point. The Fed said it had decided to raise rates in light of persisting strength in the economy. The move was aimed at extending the economic expansion and emphasised the importance of maintaining low inflation for the overall health of the economy.
THE GUARDIAN
-- ACCOUNTANT SOUGHT IN COPPER INQUIRY

The Serious Fraud Office is trying to track down Michael D Smith, a freelance accountant who worked for some British metal brokers. The SFO is having difficulties tracking the American citizen because of his common name. There is nothing to suggest Smith has done anything improper, but investigators believe he has a close knowledge of the finances of certain metals brokers who traded with rogue trader Hamanaka.
-- P AND O WARNING ON FERRY MERGER

Lord Sterling of Plaistow, the P&O chairman, has warned the Monopolies and Mergers Commission against blocking the proposed merger of its cross-Channel ferry operation with rival Stena. This comes a day after Ian Lang, President of the Board of Trade, said there would be no decisions on mergers awaiting the MMC before the general election. Sterling said it would be unlikely the plan would be blocked because it was inevitable one strong player would dominate the short-sea ferry service.
-- NUCLEAR FLAGSHIP LIMPING AT A THIRD OF CAPACITY

New figures show that British Nuclear Fuels' 2.3 billion stg Thorp plant in Cumbria is operating at less than a third of its capacity and it could take 30 years to reprocess the first 7,000 tonnes of spent reactor fuel rather than the ten years forecast. Technical difficulties are blamed. The news comes as BNFL is negotiating a merger with Magnox Electric, the country's only other state-owned nuclear company.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- PILKINGTON WARNS ON THE COST OF GERMAN CUTS

Glassmaker Pilkington has warned that profits would be 55 million stg lower this year because of the need for further redundancies and asset write-downs in Germany. Shares fell a further six per cent. Pilkington claim a collapse in flat glass prices since the start of the year and a slowdown in the German construction market meant that it would have to axe its continental operations for the second time in two years.
-- RECORD ONE BILLION STG PROPERTY SALE ROCKS HONG KONG

A residential property development in Hong Kong has been sold for 11.8 billion Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to almost one billion stg, to Sino Land, a locally listed property developer. This is believed to be a world record for a site of this kind. Analysts agreed that the purchase represented a vote of confidence in the colony's property market three months ahead of the return to Chinese sovereignty.
-- BZW DISMISSES REPORTS OF ERROR

The investment banking arm of Barclay's Bank, BZW, is playing down news of a 11.5 million stg loss on a 1996 currency trade by dismissing suggestions there had been a mispricing error, saying it was an ordinary deal which had gone wrong. BZW sources insist that the people involved were within their dealing limits and that when managers discovered a rapid movement in the currency markets they acted "within minutes".
